title: Authored events
description: The punctuation the cards don't do: a seasonal festival, a storm, DL's birthday (plan section 2, 'Layer 3: the event engine'). Where a card is drawn under a pacing target, an authored event becomes eligible when its own `trigger` is met, and while it runs it takes priority over any card named in `priorityOver` so a small random card never steps on something with a more interesting result. Reuses the card schema's `hooks`, `storybook`, `moment`, `beat` blocks and predicate shape (events.schema.json) rather than redefining them.

timeScale.description: Same shape and meaning as events.schema.json's timeScale; repeated here so this file is self-contained and does not need farm.json open beside it to make sense of durationSimMinutes.

trigger.description: How this event becomes eligible. Four shapes, picked by `kind`: a predicate list (every entry in `all` must hold, same predicate shape a card's `conditions` uses); a fixed point in the season calendar (`simDate`); a Ledger stock crossing a threshold (`stockThreshold`); or a fixed real calendar date (`realDate`, added #83). `predicates` and `stockThreshold` both carry their own `cooldownSimDays` because, unlike a card, an authored event has no `limits` block — a predicate list or a stock level can stay true for a long time (a whole drought, a whole winter), and without a cooldown the event would fire again the very next sim-minute.

oneOf.description: A point in the sim's own season cycle, given as a fraction of however long the current season turns out to be (#83: since balance/farm.json's outsideRules.seasons.calendar gives each season a seeded, varying real length, a season no longer has a fixed day count to point at). PROPOSED to sim on #40 and again on #84 same as v1 proposed recentWeather — there is no calendar concept in the sim yet, only the four-season wheel and a running day count. Recurs every time that season comes round. Not used by any of the three reference authored events today (dlBirthday moved to `realDate` on #83, a real calendar date being a better fit for a birthday); kept for a future event that should land at, say, the start or the midpoint of a season regardless of the season's actual length that year.

dayOfSeason.description: 0 is the first moment of the season, up to (not including) 1 at the season's end; e.g. 0.5 is the season's midpoint whether that season ran 81 real days or 101.

oneOf.description: New for #83: a fixed point in the real calendar, independent of the sim's season cycle — for something that means the same real date every year regardless of which sim season a given world's calendar has it fall in (Digital Luna's birthday, December 15; plan section 2, 'Time'). Eligible once a real year, around the sim moment closest to that real date; `windowSimMinutes`, if given, is how many sim minutes either side of that moment still count as a match, so a slow-ticking or paused world does not miss the day entirely. PROPOSED to sim on #84 alongside the calendar model in balance/farm.json's outsideRules.seasons.calendar.

variables.description: Authored parameters a card does not get (plan section 2): named values this event's own hooks and storybook read, that no other event shares. Deliberately open — unlike the rest of this schema, `additionalProperties` is not false here, because every authored event needs a different bag of them. Documented per event in docs/content/EVENT_DECK.md. Never put a `comment` key in here: an engine reading `Object.keys(event.variables)` would see it as a phantom parameter. The bag's own explanation belongs in the sibling `variablesComment` property instead.

priorityOver.description: Card ids, or bare parameter names such as a hook target (`mood`, `weather`), this event outranks while it runs: a named card does not fire, and a named parameter is not touched by any other card's hooks, until this event ends.

variablesComment.description: What the `variables` bag holds and why, for humans. Declared here instead of as a `comment` key inside `variables` so the open bag never carries a phantom parameter.
